newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWF boosts Australia sorghum forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWF boosts Australia sorghum forecast.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) said on Monday it had increased its forecast for Australian sorghum production in calendar 1997 to 1.11 million tonnes from 1.08 million tonnes in its January forecast.

Heavy rain in Australian sorghum areas in February arrived too late for southern Queensland or New South Wales (NSW) growers to consider increasing sorghum sowings, AWF said. Rain in these areas was sufficiently heavy to cause local flooding and some scouring of sections of sorghum crops, it said.
This had to be balanced against some extra weight going into sorghum grains that were nearly ripe and against some new heads formed from growth on secondary plant leaders, AWF said.

The sorghum harvest would be delayed by the rain, it said. The grain should be moving to markets now but was not, it added. Soils would have to dry out to allow passage of headers, trucks and tractors, then newly formed grains on secondaries had to mature and come to an acceptable grain moisture level, it said. Sorghum was being sown in Queensland as fields dried, it said.
"It is clear that growers have more enthusiasm for other cropping alternatives," AWF managing director Brian Bailey said.
These included sunflowers now and seeding wheat in March.
The domestic grains complex within Australia was trading above the export values for sorghum, AWF said.
The sorghum market in southern Queensland is A$5.00 a tonne over export values, while the domestic price in NSW is A$30.00 a tonne above export values, AWF said.
Traders who have made earlier sales at less than current values may attempt to negotiate out of contracts, it said.
Further rain and subsequent deterioration in the quality of unharvested sorghum would soften local prices, AWF said.
But expected increased demand from feedlots should continue to focus the trade on domestic markets, it said.
